texts.facts: In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 08.09.2019 at about 5 pm, petitioner/injured was driving his motorcycle bearing no. DL-3SDZ-8113 and was going to NOIDA from his home. When petitioner/injured reached at pusta road, Jaitpur in front of Garib yar dargah, Khadda Colony, suddenly offending vehicle in question driven by R-1 Jitender Singh came in rash and negligent manner and hit petitioner's motorcycle. Due to the same, he fell down on the ground and received grievous injuries. It is further stated that driver offending vehicle fled away from the spot and one passers-by called his brother who called the police. 3. Injured was taken to Appollo hospital where medical treatment was given to him and his MLC was prepared. He further stated that he can identify the driver of offending vehicle. 4. Thereafter FIR in question u/s 279/338 IPC was registered in this case. Further, as per record, charge-sheet for the same offence is also filed against respondent no.1. 5. Further, as per record on the first date driver-cum-owner Sudhir Kumar Upadhyay/R-1 appeared. But, as per record, he did not file any reply. 6. Further, as per record, even insurance company did not file any legal offer nor filed any reply. But contested the present DAR on the ground that MACT No. 963/19 Mohd. Wasim v. Bajaj Allianz Gen. Ins. Page No. :3: driver-cum-owner/R-1 did not had permit and TSR was new which is clear from DAR itself. As such, recovery rights are claimed by insurance company. It is further stated that as victim did not had driving licence at the time of accident, therefore, there is contributory negligence on the part of victim also. 7. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 23.01.2021 by Predecessor of this Tribunal: 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident dated 08.09.2021 involving vehicle bearing Engine number 86748 and chasis no. 3420 driven and owned by R1 and insured with R2 due to rash and negligent driving of R1 ? OPP 2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?OPP 3. Relief. 8. Petitioner tendered his examination-in-chief by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents including medical bills and medical documents including MLC Ex. PW-1/1 to PW-1/4 (colly). He was cross-examined by learned counsel for insurance company. 9. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. 10. None of the respondent led any evidence. Further, Written submissions in Form VIB filed by petitioner. 15. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident.

To avoid its liability towards the insured, the insurer has to prove that the insured was guilty of negligence and failed to exercise reasonable care in the matter of fulfilling the condition of the policy regarding use of vehicles by a duly licensed driver or one who was not disqualified to drive at the relevant time. The Tribunals in interpreting the policy conditions would apply "the rule of main purpose" and the concept of "fundamental breach" to allow defences available to the insurer under Section 149(2) of the Act. Jaibir Singh & Ors whereby the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has formulated MACAD(Motor Accident Claims Annunity Deposit Scheme) which has been made effective from 01.01.2019. The State Bank of India, Saket Courts, Delhi is directed to disburse the amount in accordance with MACAD formulated by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi. Apportionment:- 40. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: Mohd. Wasim vs Sudhir Kumar Upadhyay on 22 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143601246/ 13 " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". In the case of illiterate claimants, the Tribunal is allowed to consider the request for lumpsum payment for effecting purchase of any movable property such as agricultural implements, rickshaws etc. to earn a living. However, in such cases, the Tribunal shall make sure that the amount is actually spent for the purpose and MACT No. 963/19 Mohd. Wasim v. Bajaj Allianz Gen. Ins. Page No. 19 of 24 BK the demand is not a ruse to withdraw money. In the case of semi- illiterate claimants, the Tribunal should ordinarily invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit. But if the Tribunal is satisfied for reasons to be stated in writing that the whole or part of the amount is required for expanding an existing business or for purchasing some property for earning a livelihood, the Tribunal can release the whole or part of the amount of compensation to the claimant provided the Tribunal will ensure that the amount is invested for the purpose for which it is demanded and paid. Moreover, in the case of literate persons, the Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i) only if, having regard to the age, fiscal background and strata of the society to which the claimant belongs and such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks that in the larger interest of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded, it is necessary to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit. Thus, sufficient discretion has been given to the Tribunal not to insist on investment of the compensation amount in long term fixed deposit and to release even the whole amount in the case of literate persons.
